question: Which part of the brain acts as the body's natural thermostat during a fever?

options.A: Cerebellum
options.B: Hypothalamus
options.C: Thalamus
options.D: Medulla oblongata

explanation: The hypothalamus is like the internal thermostat in your brain. It turns up the heat when your body needs to fight off an infection. [learn more](GST114_U4_T4#GST114_U4_T4_h5)

question: What is a very common physical change patients notice after they start eating a healthier diet?

options.A: Immediate growth in height as an adult
options.B: Permanent loss of the need for sleep
options.C: Reduced fatigue and higher energy levels
options.D: Complete immunity to all viral infections

explanation: You got it! Giving the body proper fuel works wonders—patients are often amazed at how much lighter and more energetic they feel. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T003#GNS227_U7_T003_h6)

question: What is a must-have when introducing a complex new clinical workflow?

options.A: Protected time for staff training during working hours
options.B: Cutting down the number of patient admissions
options.C: Firing senior nurses to save on salaries
options.D: Buying luxury furniture for the breakroom

explanation: Exactly! You can't expect nurses to master new workflows on top of an already crazy shift without giving them dedicated time to learn. [learn more](GST319_U1_T4#GST319_U1_T4_h6)

question: Why must a laboratory result always be compared with the patient's physical condition?

options.A: Laboratory machines are always broken
options.B: Patients usually lie about their symptoms
options.C: Lab values alone do not tell the whole clinical story
options.D: Doctors refuse to read raw lab reports

explanation: A number on a lab sheet is only one piece of the puzzle and must match how the patient actually feels and looks. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T4#GNS124_U6_T4_h3)

question: What is the main use of a run chart in quality improvement?

options.A: To record patient medical diagnoses in an emergency
options.B: To schedule holiday shifts for nurses
options.C: To display data points over time and track performance trends
options.D: To calculate annual salaries for hospital staff

explanation: Spot on! Run charts plot data chronologically so you can see at a glance whether your ward's new interventions are actually improving things. [learn more](GST319_U1_T4#GST319_U1_T4_h7)

question: What does information asymmetry mean in the context of healthcare?

options.A: All treatment prices are publicly displayed online
options.B: Patients have equal access to medical textbooks
options.C: Providers know much more about medicine than patients
options.D: Governments hide medical research from the public

explanation: Information asymmetry describes the unequal knowledge gap between trained health professionals and everyday consumers. [learn more](GST322_U1_T4#GST322_U1_T4_h3)

question: A patient is moved from a rural clinic to a big city hospital with incompatible software. What is the biggest safety risk?

options.A: Critical allergy and medication history may be delayed or missing
options.B: Nurses will be forced to perform physical examinations outdoors
options.C: The patient room will lose electricity due to software overload
options.D: The patient will automatically be billed twice for their hospital stay

explanation: Spot on! When systems can't talk to each other, vital details like drug allergies can get lost in translation during transfers. Excellent clinical thinking! [learn more](GNS113_U2_T3#GNS113_U2_T3_h6)

question: Why do teenage girls need more daily iron in their diet than younger children do?

options.A: To prevent soft bones from a lack of sunlight
options.B: To support monthly period blood loss and growing muscles
options.C: To maintain normal skin color and elasticity
options.D: To help digest heavy local meals easily

explanation: You nailed it! Monthly periods and rapid physical growth use up iron quickly, so eating more iron-rich foods helps prevent anemia. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T010#GNS227_U2_T010_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of using a guide like the Iowa Model in nursing?

options.A: To punish nurses who refuse to follow new guidelines
options.B: To calculate the monthly financial budget of the hospital
options.C: To help researchers write better scientific articles
options.D: To provide a step-by-step roadmap for making clinical changes

explanation: Well done! Models like the Iowa Model give us a clear, friendly roadmap to follow from the moment we spot a problem to when we check if our change worked. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T3#GNS224_U4_T3_h3)

question: When moving a heavy medication cart down a hospital hallway, what is the safest technique?

options.A: Pull the cart behind you for better steering
options.B: Hold the cart with only one hand at all times
options.C: Push the cart rather than pulling it
options.D: Run quickly to minimize the duration of the push

explanation: You got it! Pushing lets you use your body weight and strong leg muscles instead of straining your back and shoulders. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h5)

question: What is an epidemiological reservoir in simple terms?

options.A: A temporary holding tank for treated hospital waste
options.B: The natural home where a germ normally lives and multiplies
options.C: A man-made chemical used to destroy harmful bacteria
options.D: The sterile medical equipment used during surgery

explanation: Think of a reservoir as the natural hangout spot where a pathogen lives, grows, and multiplies so it can stick around over time! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T80#GNS214_U1_T80_h1)

question: What is a major way non-governmental organizations (NGOs) help in healthcare?

options.A: Controlling the licensure of medical doctors and nurses
options.B: Collecting taxes from local citizens to fund state budgets
options.C: Replacing all national laws with private organizational rules
options.D: Filling service gaps left by underfunded public systems

explanation: When public resources fall short, NGOs often step in with extra supplies, outreach, and hands-on help for communities in need. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T6#GNS123_U6_T6_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of using orthopedic traction?

options.A: To apply a pulling force to align bones and reduce spasms
options.B: To completely immobilize the patient without using any bed sheets
options.C: To permanently replace damaged joint cartilage without surgery
options.D: To deliver strong local pain medication directly into a fracture

explanation: Traction uses a steady pull on body parts to restore bone alignment, stretch tight muscles, and ease painful spasms before definitive repair. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T7#GNS221_U1_T7_h1)

question: Which of these is a classic input device you might use while giving medications?

options.A: A bedside monitor screen
options.B: A laser printer
options.C: An emergency alarm speaker
options.D: A barcode scanner

explanation: Spot on! Input devices 'feed' information into the computer. Scanning a patient's wristband sends their details straight into the system. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T7#GNS113_U1_T7_h2)

question: Why must an effective screening program have accessible treatment available?

options.A: Treatment reduces the cost of running the laboratory
options.B: Patients will refuse to take the test otherwise
options.C: It proves the screening test is completely infallible
options.D: Finding a disease is useless if patients cannot get care

explanation: Screening only improves health outcomes if positive results lead to timely, effective medical interventions. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T4#GNS225_U2_T4_h3)

question: On a scatter diagram, what does a single dot represent?

options.A: The total average of all patients in the study
options.B: The error rate of the measuring instrument
options.C: The difference between two hospital wards
options.D: One subject's values for both variables combined

explanation: Each dot is like a snapshot for one individual participant, showing both of their measurements meeting at a point. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T12#GNS217_U4_T12_h3)

question: Why is checking on the emotional wellbeing of a patient in long-term traction a key part of your nursing care?

options.A: Anxious patients always disconnect their own traction
options.B: Good mental support replaces the need for pain meds
options.C: Stress stops bones from absorbing calcium
options.D: Being stuck in one position for weeks often brings down their mood and causes stress

explanation: Brilliant insight! Lying still for weeks takes a heavy emotional toll. Being a warm, listening ear is just as important as managing their physical injuries. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T7#GNS221_U1_T7_h6)

question: Why do nurses look beyond the obvious symptoms when a patient's condition is crashing?

options.A: To ensure the hospital billing department receives correct insurance data
options.B: Because lab technicians require secondary confirmation for all tests
options.C: So that family members can be discharged home earlier in the shift
options.D: Because primary organ failure quickly triggers a cascade affecting other systems

explanation: When one major organ starts failing, it quickly pulls other vital systems down with it. Checking the whole patient keeps you steps ahead! [learn more](GNS315_U2_T4#GNS315_U2_T4_h1)

question: What happens to the heart muscle when it has to pump blood against a tight, narrowed valve for a long time?

options.A: The muscle walls thin out and become weak
options.B: The heart electrical system stops completely
options.C: The muscle thickens due to the heavy workload
options.D: The heart chambers stretch out instantly without any wall changes

explanation: Pumping against a narrowed valve is hard work! The heart muscle responds by growing thicker (hypertrophy) to handle the extra resistance. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T12#GNS213_U1_T12_h6)

question: As a bedside nurse, why are you considered right at the center of hospital waste management?

options.A: Nurses are the only staff members allowed to touch trash
options.B: Nurses are legally liable for the city waste trucks
options.C: Nurses generate waste during daily patient care activities
options.D: Hospital management forces nurses to pay for disposal bins

explanation: Spot on! Because we give direct patient care every day, we are the first ones to handle and discard medical materials. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T16#GNS122_U3_T16_h1)

question: Which lab tests do nurses commonly check to assess a patient's kidney function before giving medications?

options.A: Serum creatinine and BUN
options.B: ALT and AST liver enzymes
options.C: Red blood cell count and platelets
options.D: Sodium and potassium levels only

explanation: Blood Urea Nitrogen (BUN) and serum creatinine are your go-to lab markers. Checking these lets you know if the kidneys are clearing waste properly before piling on extra medications. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T4#GNS125_U1_T4_h8)

question: Which action represents effective nursing advocacy in food policy?

options.A: Personally financing the national agricultural subsidy budget
options.B: Sharing clinical data with policymakers to support nutritional programs
options.C: Refusing to care for patients who eat unhealthy processed foods
options.D: Replacing all government food inspectors with hospital nurses

explanation: Nurses use their clinical insights to influence decision-makers and support programs that improve community health. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T028#GNS227_U2_T028_h8)

question: Which of these is NOT a safe nursing practice when dealing with antagonistic medications?

options.A: Observing the patient for expected therapeutic reversal of toxicity
options.B: Checking full medication lists for accidental drug cancellations
options.C: Ignoring herbal remedies because they do not interact with hospital drugs
options.D: Understanding whether an antagonist is competitive or non-competitive

explanation: Never ignore herbal supplements! Many herbs can mess with hospital medications through unexpected chemical or drug interactions. Always check the full list! [learn more](GNS125_U5_T7#GNS125_U5_T7_h6)

question: How do Electronic Health Records help different healthcare workers team up better?

options.A: By automatically assigning daily nursing tasks to the available staff on duty
options.B: By restricting access to client files to only one department at a time
options.C: By allowing authorized clinicians from various specialties to review up-to-date findings instantly
options.D: By replacing verbal shift handovers with automated text messages

explanation: When everyone can see the latest test results and notes right away, the whole care team stays on the same page without delays. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T4#GNS113_U3_T4_h2)

question: What is the very first thing you should do before making any hospital bed?

options.A: Strip all the old linens off the mattress simultaneously
options.B: Lock the bed wheels and adjust it to a comfortable working height
options.C: Ask the patient to stand up and walk around the ward
options.D: Remove all pillows and place them on a nearby chair

explanation: Correct! Safety first: lock the wheels so the bed doesn't roll away, and raise it so you don't hurt your back while working. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T3#GNS112_U4_T3_h6)

question: What is the main goal of electrical cardioversion for a patient with a rapid, dangerous heart rhythm?

options.A: To permanently destroy the atrioventricular node
options.B: To reset the heart back to a normal sinus rhythm
options.C: To measure the exact cardiac output of the ventricles
options.D: To widen narrowed coronary arteries instantly

explanation: Cardioversion is like hitting 'restart' on a glitchy computer. It delivers a timed electrical shock to stop the chaos and let the heart's natural pacemaker take back control. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T3#GNS213_U1_T3_h6)

question: A community nurse is inspecting a pregnant woman's home delivery kit. Which item is UNNECESSARY or unsafe for newborn cord care?

options.A: A clean, sterile razor blade for cutting the cord
options.B: Traditional herbal mixture applied directly to the cut cord
options.C: Clean thread to tie off the umbilical cord securely
options.D: Soap and clean water for thorough handwashing

explanation: Applying unsterile substances like herbal mixtures to the umbilical cord introduces bacteria and causes severe neonatal infections like tetanus. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T15#GNS324_U3_T15_h2)

question: Which baby health problems are most common when born to teenage mothers?

options.A: Congenital heart murmurs caused by maternal stress
options.B: Advanced bone maturation at birth
options.C: Premature birth and low birth weight
options.D: Excessive birth weight and overgrown organs

explanation: Spot on! Because the mother's body is still growing, babies often arrive too early and small. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T13#GNS312_U1_T13_h5)

question: What does 'disseminating research findings' mean?

options.A: Destroying all raw data once the graduation grade is posted
options.B: Hiding the final report in a private locker so no one copies it
options.C: Sharing the results through publications, conferences, or presentations
options.D: Translating the clinical report into multiple foreign languages

explanation: Dissemination just means spreading the good news! Getting your findings out to other nurses via journals or talks improves patient care everywhere. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T17#GNS217_U3_T17_h10)

question: What is the most important home adjustment to prevent falls for an older adult using a walker?

options.A: Adding heavy carpets to cushion potential falls
options.B: Installing overhead lighting in every single room
options.C: Removing loose throw rugs and cluttered pathways
options.D: Replacing all standard furniture with hospital beds

explanation: Clear floors mean safer walking! Loose rugs are a major trap for walker tips and wheels, so clearing them out is a top priority. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T4#GNS221_U1_T4_h7)

question: How do nurses accurately measure fluid output from a heavy surgical dressing or pad?

options.A: Estimating the stain size using a common ruler
options.B: Squeezing the fluid out into a measuring cup
options.C: Asking the patient how much fluid they think leaked
options.D: Weighing the wet item and subtracting the dry weight

explanation: Weight is the most reliable way to quantify fluid soaked into solid materials, where one gram roughly equals one milliliter. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T19#GNS122_U1_T19_h5)

question: Why should you always encourage a patient on a high-protein diet to drink plenty of water?

options.A: It replaces the electrolytes lost through the skin
options.B: It slows down the digestion of amino acids in the stomach
options.C: It helps the kidneys clear extra nitrogen waste products
options.D: It prevents the patient from feeling hungry too often

explanation: Breaking down proteins produces urea and nitrogen waste that pass through the kidneys. Extra fluids protect the kidneys from working too hard and prevent dehydration! [learn more](GNS227_U6_T003#GNS227_U6_T003_h6)

question: What is the number one thing that encourages young people to open up and share sensitive health info with a nurse?

options.A: Free mobile phones
options.B: Presence of tribal leaders
options.C: Free meals at the clinic
options.D: Guaranteed confidentiality

explanation: Trust is everything! Teens need to know their secrets are safe with you before they'll feel comfortable talking about their health. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T48#GNS214_U1_T48_h3)

question: What is a major reason families ask health workers to perform FGM?

options.A: Government laws require a medical certificate for marriage
options.B: Fear of social stigma and community rejection
options.C: Traditional cutters are no longer available in cities
options.D: Doctors charge much lower fees than traditional cutters

explanation: Deep cultural beliefs and fear of exclusion drive families to seek out the procedure to secure their daughters' social standing. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T5#GNS312_U1_T5_h2)

question: What is metaplasia?

options.A: An abnormal decrease in the total number of cells in an organ
options.B: The complete death of tissue due to a lack of oxygen supply
options.C: The replacement of one mature cell type by another mature cell type
options.D: Uncontrolled cell division that forms a malignant tumor mass

explanation: Metaplasia is a reversible adaptation where one adult cell type swaps for another type better suited to handle ongoing stress. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T10#GNS111_U1_T10_h5)

question: Which condition is a PET scan often used to help evaluate?

options.A: A simple hairline skull fracture
options.B: Bleeding right after a car crash
options.C: Alzheimer's disease and seizure focus points
options.D: Spinal pressure from a slipped disc

explanation: PET scans show changes in brain energy use, which helps doctors spot conditions like Alzheimer's or epilepsy. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T8#GNS222_U3_T8_h5)

question: A nurse notices a sudden jump in malaria cases during the rainy season. What kind of transmission is this?

options.A: Foodborne
options.B: Waterborne
options.C: Vector-borne
options.D: Airborne

explanation: Spot on! Malaria is spread by mosquitoes (the vector), which love to breed in the puddles formed during the rainy season. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T85#GNS214_U1_T85_h2)

question: How do heavy psychosocial struggles in one family member usually affect the whole household?

options.A: They lower household utility bills by reducing daily home activity
options.B: They automatically improve the communication skills of other relatives
options.C: They have no impact as long as the patient stays inside their room
options.D: They create financial strain and emotional exhaustion for everyone

explanation: Well done! Mental distress doesn't happen in a vacuum. It often leads to caregiver fatigue and puts a heavy emotional and financial load on the family. [learn more](GNS314_U6_T2#GNS314_U6_T2_h3)

question: Why is continuous electronic fetal monitoring so important during preterm labour?

options.A: Preterm fetuses tolerate the stress of contractions poorly
options.B: It stops the progress of cervical dilation automatically
options.C: It is the only way to calculate the exact due date
options.D: It prevents the mother from experiencing any back pain

explanation: Preterm babies have delicate reserves, so watching the monitor closely helps us catch signs of distress early. You're learning top-tier patient safety! [learn more](GNS226_U4_T001#GNS226_U4_T001_h7)

question: A nurse wants to test a new pain reassessment workflow. Which of these is the best way to start a small-scale test?

options.A: Implement the workflow across all regional hospitals starting next Monday
options.B: Wait until next year when more funding becomes available
options.C: Test the workflow with three patients on the morning shift with one assigned nurse
options.D: Ask every nurse in the country to write an essay on pain reassessment

explanation: Spot on! Testing with just a few patients and a single nurse lets you see how the workflow feels in real life without creating chaos. [learn more](GST319_U3_T4#GST319_U3_T4_h4)

question: A patient from a local community frequently visits the clinic complaining of severe body aches and fatigue, but medical tests find no physical cause. What should the nurse consider?

options.A: Physical complaints can never be linked to psychological stress
options.B: The patient is definitely fabricating symptoms to get prescription drugs
options.C: The laboratory equipment is likely malfunctioning and needs calibration
options.D: The patient might be expressing emotional distress through physical symptoms

explanation: Many individuals culturally communicate psychological distress through physical symptoms, requiring nurses to look beyond pure medical lab results. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T7#GNS314_U1_T7_h4)

question: What is the most important first step when a patient rings the bell asking for nausea medication?

options.A: Encourage the patient to drink large volumes of cold water
options.B: Immediately administer a broad-spectrum 5-HT3 antagonist IV
options.C: Assess the character, frequency, and potential triggers of the nausea
options.D: Insert a nasogastric tube to decompress the stomach

explanation: Spot on! Always assess first before giving meds. Understanding what's causing the nausea helps you pick the right treatment and catch hidden dangers. Excellent nursing judgment! [learn more](GNS223_U3_T6#GNS223_U3_T6_h7)

question: Which kidney condition frequently relies on the intraperitoneal route for daily management?

options.A: Peritoneal dialysis
options.B: Total parenteral nutrition
options.C: Intramuscular immunization
options.D: Intravenous hydration

explanation: You nailed it! Peritoneal dialysis uses the patient's own belly lining as a natural filter when their kidneys can no longer clean the blood. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T11#GNS125_U3_T11_h4)

question: Which symptom is a classic peripheral adverse effect of anticholinergic drugs?

options.A: Watery diarrhea
options.B: Dry mouth
options.C: Narrowed pupils
options.D: Excessive drooling

explanation: Blocking parasympathetic activity decreases saliva production, leading to noticeable dry mouth. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T7#GNS223_U6_T7_h5)

question: What is the best way for a nurse to provide psychological first aid to a disaster victim?

options.A: Encouraging the victim to forget the event and focus on rebuilding
options.B: Offering a calm presence and active listening without false promises
options.C: Leaving the victim alone immediately so they can process their grief
options.D: Telling the victim that everything will quickly return to normal

explanation: Wonderful! Psychological first aid is all about being present, listening patiently, and supporting them without making promises you can't keep. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T3#GNS315_U5_T3_h8)

question: What is the main difference between hygiene factors and motivators in Herzberg's theory?

options.A: Motivators are about physical health, while hygiene factors are about pay
options.B: Hygiene factors apply only to doctors, while motivators apply to nurses
options.C: Hygiene factors prevent dissatisfaction, while motivators drive true engagement
options.D: Hygiene factors guarantee promotion, while motivators prevent illness

explanation: Good pay and working conditions stop us from complaining (hygiene), but doing meaningful work is what truly makes us love the job (motivators). [learn more](GST321_U3_T7#GST321_U3_T7_h2)

question: Why do clinicians often use resting metabolic rate (RMR) instead of basal metabolic rate (BMR)?

options.A: It completely excludes the energy used by internal organs
options.B: It is always identical to total daily energy expenditure
options.C: It measures the exact calories burned during running
options.D: It requires fewer strict laboratory conditions to measure

explanation: Great job! RMR is much more practical in hospital and clinic settings because it doesn't force the patient to go through a strict 12-hour fast and absolute rest like BMR does. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T008#GNS227_U4_T008_h2)

question: Why is getting an accurate diagnosis so important before treating any vaginal infection?

options.A: All vaginal infections automatically resolve on their own within forty-eight hours
options.B: Over-the-counter creams permanently damage normal vaginal tissue if used incorrectly
options.C: Treatments vary completely depending on whether the cause is bacterial, fungal, or parasitic
options.D: Providers cannot prescribe any medication without a blood test confirming the infection

explanation: Makes total sense, right? Antifungals cure yeast, antibiotics treat bacteria, and anti-parasitics handle trich. Using the wrong drug won't help our patient at all! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T10#GNS216_U5_T10_h5)

question: What emotional feeling do patients adjusting to a new stoma most commonly experience?

options.A: Complete indifference to physical changes
options.B: Immediate excitement to rush back to work
options.C: Angry behavior toward medical staff
options.D: Body image disturbance and anxiety

explanation: Spot on. Adjusting to a changed body appearance and worrying about leaks or smells can easily cause stress and emotional upset. You're doing great! [learn more](GNS212_U1_T14#GNS212_U1_T14_h7)

question: A sudden malaria outbreak brings a flood of new patients to the ward. Which expense will go up as a result?

options.A: Fixed costs like the monthly rent for the hospital building
options.B: Fixed costs like the long-term equipment lease payments
options.C: Fixed costs like the baseline administrative software license
options.D: Variable costs like disposable syringes and malaria test kits

explanation: More patients mean you need more test kits and syringes! These items change (vary) directly with patient volume. [learn more](GST322_U2_T2#GST322_U2_T2_h4)

question: A patient swallowed a small toy that got stuck in their throat. Why would a doctor perform a laryngoscopy?

options.A: To test the patient's swallowing reflex
options.B: To locate and safely remove the inhaled object
options.C: To measure the oxygen content in the lungs
options.D: To check for chronic bacterial throat infections

explanation: Spot on! When something gets stuck where it shouldn't be, this procedure lets the clinician spot the object and safely take it out. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T4#GNS221_U2_T4_h2)

question: What important step is needed right after using ethylene oxide gas on medical items?

options.A: Immediate rinsing in sterile water and drying
options.B: Submersion in a neutralizing acid bath
options.C: Exposure to ultraviolet light rays
options.D: Thorough aeration to remove toxic gas residues

explanation: Ethylene oxide gas is toxic to human tissue, so items must air out thoroughly in a special cabinet before anyone touches them. [learn more](GST114_U2_T11#GST114_U2_T11_h4)

question: What two main areas of human life does MHPSS focus on combining?

options.A: Economic and political dimensions
options.B: Physical and spiritual dimensions
options.C: Pharmacological and surgical dimensions
options.D: Psychological and social dimensions

explanation: You've got this! MHPSS stands for Mental Health and Psychosocial Support. It brings together how a person feels inside (psychological) and how they relate to their community and relationships (social). [learn more](GNS314_U6_T1#GNS314_U6_T1_h1)

question: Which nursing action best demonstrates proper infection control during an injection?

options.A: Placing used needles on the bedside table for later disposal
options.B: Avoiding touching the sterile needle shaft or plunger tip
options.C: Reusing the same alcohol swab for multiple patients to save supplies
options.D: Recapping used needles immediately using both hands

explanation: Keeping sterile parts untouched prevents contamination and protects the patient from localized or systemic infections. [learn more](GNS125_U4_T2#GNS125_U4_T2_h6)

question: Why is educational informatics particularly useful when clinical placement sites are scarce?

options.A: It automates the grading of physical bedside nursing procedures
options.B: It provides virtual patient scenarios to practice clinical reasoning
options.C: It allows students to skip graduation exams and start working early
options.D: It completely replaces the need for licensed nursing faculty

explanation: Simulation and virtual tools give students valuable practice in decision-making when real clinical wards are overcrowded. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T2#GNS113_U1_T2_h4)

question: Which hormone unlocks cells so glucose can move in from the blood?

options.A: Insulin
options.B: Glucagon
options.C: Thyroxine
options.D: Cortisol

explanation: Think of insulin as the golden key that unlocks cell doors, letting glucose step inside from the bloodstream to provide energy. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T010#GNS227_U1_T010_h4)

question: You prepare a total volume of 24 mL to run over 24 hours. What should you set the hourly rate to?

options.A: 1.0 mL per hour
options.B: 24.0 mL per hour
options.C: 12.0 mL per hour
options.D: 48.0 mL per hour

explanation: You're a star at math! 24 mL divided by 24 hours gives you a neat and steady rate of 1.0 mL per hour. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T4#GNS212_U4_T4_h4)

question: Which of these is a major characteristic of adult learners during a teaching session?

options.A: They refuse to participate in group discussions or role play
options.B: They remember long lists of medical terms better than children
options.C: They need strict discipline and constant supervision from lecturers
options.D: They prefer to be actively involved in planning their learning goals

explanation: Brilliant! Adults love having a say in what and how they learn. They value their independence rather than just sitting quietly as passive listeners. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T10#GNS124_U5_T10_h2)

question: Why are elderly adults usually more at risk for catching infections?

options.A: Their skin becomes completely impermeable
options.B: Their immune defenses decline with age
options.C: They consume too many hospital medications
options.D: They have faster cellular regeneration

explanation: As people age, the immune system naturally slows down a bit, making it easier for germs to take hold. Great job thinking about your patients' vulnerability! [learn more](GNS313_U2_T11#GNS313_U2_T11_h1)

question: Which heart rhythm do adults in sudden cardiac arrest show most often?

options.A: Atrial flutter
options.B: First-degree heart block
options.C: Ventricular fibrillation
options.D: Sinus bradycardia

explanation: Quality control is key! Testing the plates beforehand makes sure our materials are in top shape before real patient samples arrive. [learn more](GST114_U5_T4#GST114_U5_T4_h7)

question: A patient runs out of insulin two weeks after a storm destroys nearby pharmacies. What type of disaster impact is this?

options.C: Indirect impact
options.D: Direct impact

question: In antenatal care, what does BPCR stand for?

options.C: Basic Physiological Childbirth Routine
options.D: Blood Pressure and Cardiac Response

explanation: You've got it! BPCR is all about helping families plan ahead for a normal delivery and know what to do if an emergency pops up. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T007#GNS226_U1_T007_h5)

question: A nursing team notices surgical site infections have gone up over two quarters. What should they do next?

options.A: Stop tracking infections so the report looks clean for management
options.B: Design and test a corrective intervention, then monitor the infection rates again
options.C: Blame the patients for having poor personal hygiene at home
options.D: Wait five years before taking any action on the infection data

explanation: Quality improvement is a loop: spot the issue, try a fix, and check back to see if your fix worked. You're thinking like a clinical leader! [learn more](GST319_U4_T5#GST319_U4_T5_h7)

question: Why is keeping an eye on intracranial pressure (ICP) so vital after a severe head injury?

options.A: To prevent the patient from experiencing chronic back pain
options.B: To determine when the patient is ready for solid foods
options.C: To calculate the exact number of calories the brain burns daily
options.D: To make sure enough blood flows to the brain despite swelling

explanation: When the brain swells inside the skull, high pressure can pinch blood vessels closed and cut off vital oxygen. Monitoring helps us prevent brain starvation. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T3#GNS321_U2_T3_h7)

question: Using the Rule of Nines, what percentage of the total body surface area does an adult's entire front chest and abdomen (anterior trunk) cover?

options.A: 36 percent
options.B: 18 percent
options.C: 9 percent
options.D: 27 percent

question: A nurse quietly grumbles about a patient's abortion while making her bed. Which important standard of care is the nurse breaking?

options.A: The legal requirement for mandatory police reporting
options.B: Strict adherence to hospital administrative policies
options.C: Unconditional positive regard and non-maleficence
options.D: The principle of client autonomy over surgical choices

question: What is the main task of cytotoxic T-cells?

options.A: Producing free-floating antibodies in the blood plasma

options.C: Filtering waste materials out of the lymphatic fluid
options.D: Producing new red blood cells inside the bone marrow

question: What is a major part of helping a pregnant client make a practical birth plan?

options.A: Arranging transportation and identifying the place of delivery

options.C: Choosing the exact college the child will attend later

explanation: A good birth plan solves logistics! Knowing how she will get to the hospital and exactly which health facility she is going to prevents dangerous delays during labor. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h7)

question: How should a nurse manager guide a brand-new student nurse doing a complex procedure for the very first time?

options.A: With complete independence and no supervision
options.B: With close supervision and clear, step-by-step guidance
options.C: By ignoring the procedure until the shift ends
options.D: By delegating the task entirely to another student

explanation: Beginners need high support and a watchful eye to keep patients safe and build their confidence. You'd want the same when learning a new skill! [learn more](GST321_U3_T2#GST321_U3_T2_h4)

question: Why does the Model for Improvement focus on small tests of change rather than massive overhauls?

options.A: Hospital management bans large projects due to budget constraints
options.B: Small tests reduce risk and let staff see if a change works before spreading it
options.C: Regulatory bodies only permit one minor change per year
options.D: Patients refuse to participate in large-scale hospital studies

explanation: Spot on! Testing things on a small scale lets nurses safely try out new ideas without disrupting the whole ward. [learn more](GST319_U2_T8#GST319_U2_T8_h1)

question: Which ancient group regularly practiced fasting and purging because they believed bad food caused all illnesses?

options.A: Ancient Egyptians
options.B: Modern Nigerians
options.C: The British Empire
options.D: Ancient Romans

question: A clinic is starting a digital triage system but keeps paper registers nearby just in case the network goes down. What is this strategy called?

options.A: Outcome measurement
options.B: Stakeholder engagement
options.C: Risk mitigation
options.D: Aim setting

explanation: You've got this! Having a reliable backup plan for when things go wrong (like poor internet or power cuts) is called risk mitigation. [learn more](GST319_U3_T1#GST319_U3_T1_h6)

question: What is the main focus of a community diagnosis?

options.A: The health status of an entire population
options.B: The medical history of individual clinic staff
options.C: The recovery rate of a single hospital patient
options.D: The financial budget of a local health clinic

explanation: Spot on! Unlike individual care where you treat one patient at a time, a community diagnosis looks at the overall health picture of an entire group of people. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T18#GNS225_U2_T18_h1)

question: Why is addiction considered a chronic brain disease instead of just a lack of willpower?

options.A: It permanently alters brain circuits related to reward and self-control
options.B: It only affects people with inherited genetic weaknesses in their lungs
options.C: It completely stops the liver from producing digestive enzymes
options.D: It causes immediate physical paralysis in every single user

explanation: Think of it this way: long-term substance use physically changes how the brain's wiring works, making self-control super difficult without proper support. It's a health condition, not a character flaw! [learn more](GNS125_U4_T3#GNS125_U4_T3_h1)

question: What is typical for a patient with a spinal cord injury located above the sacral micturition center?

options.A: Complete inability of the kidneys to filter blood

question: When a patient reaches the end of life, what is the main focus of nursing care?

options.A: Restricting family visits to maintain strict silence

options.C: Focusing only on lab values and medication charts
options.D: Ensuring a peaceful, pain-free, and dignified transition

question: How do standard expectorants typically trigger increased fluid secretion in the lungs?

question: Why shouldn't healthcare workers hand-wash contaminated Lassa patient linens in open basins?

options.A: Modern detergents are too expensive for primary clinics

options.C: Washing powder damages the fabric of hospital bedsheets

question: What usually happens on the ward when a nurse struggles with poor time management?

options.C: Increased risk of missed care and medication errors

question: What happens to body cells when a hypotonic IV solution is infused into the vascular system?

question: What is the main difference between intentional and unintentional non-adherence?

options.A: Intentional non-adherence is caused solely by forgetfulness or confusion

options.C: Intentional non-adherence is a deliberate choice by the patient to alter or skip doses
options.D: Unintentional non-adherence only happens with expensive imported drugs

explanation: Patients practice intentional non-adherence when they knowingly decide not to take their drugs due to side effects, cost, or personal beliefs. Unintentional non-adherence stems from factors like forgetfulness or physical inability to manage the regimen. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T2#GNS215_U4_T2_h1)

question: What was the early nature of psychiatric facilities like the Yaba Lunatic Asylum when first opened?

question: What is the highest possible value for a correlation coefficient?

question: Which post-sigmoidoscopy symptom means a patient might have a bowel perforation and needs emergency care?

question: When is the best time for a nurse to document that a medication was given?

question: What is a major danger of having bad sanitation and broken toilets in a school?

question: A patient with unsteady balance prepares for discharge home. What is the best nursing action to address home safety?

question: Why is healthcare different from buying regular goods at the market?

question: Why is regular communication between the home health nurse and the physical therapist so important?

question: Why does the mother's uterine lining change into 'decidua' cells during early pregnancy?

options.B: To close the cervical os tightly during early pregnancy

question: Why is the digital divide a big hurdle in modern nursing education?

question: How does the placenta give a newborn temporary protection against common infections?

question: During transport, who is mainly responsible for checking vital signs and giving medications?

question: What is the main function of a Clinical Decision Support System (CDSS)?

question: Why do antigen-presenting cells need to display pieces of a germ on MHC molecules?

options.B: Innate white blood cells need MHC to digest food particles safely
options.C: Pathogens use MHC markers to hide from circulating macrophages

question: Which of these is most likely done in a standard general operating theatre?

question: Why must men with an enlarged prostate be very careful with central anticholinergics?

question: What is the primary job of cytotoxic T cells?

question: Why must a nurse catch postpartum infections early?

question: Why are community health workers so helpful in managing family planning defaulters?

question: Why is cultural humility important when providing dietary advice?

options.B: Food carries deep emotional and cultural meaning for patients

options.D: It proves to the doctor that the nurse is well-traveled

question: Why is putting in a large-bore intravenous (IV) line such an urgent priority when managing severe PPH?

options.C: To allow rapid running of IV fluids and blood products
options.D: To monitor central venous pressure continuously

question: Why is treating an infected person usually not enough to stop a parasite outbreak on its own?

options.B: Parasites mutate into viral pathogens inside the human host
options.C: Laboratory tests cannot confirm when a patient is cured

question: Why must nurse managers review monthly financial reports?

options.D: To calculate the annual bonus for the hospital's chief executive officer

question: As a nurse, which action best protects a research participant's confidentiality?

question: When there's no institutional funding for a nursing study, what do nurses often end up doing?

options.B: Rely entirely on free pharmaceutical samples

question: A nurse manager has limited funds for a ward. Which item should be bought first to keep patients safe?

options.C: Foreign travel allowances for senior administrative staff members

question: Why would a patient with a severe drug overdose and low consciousness urgently need a mechanical ventilator?

options.C: Reversal of metabolic acidosis
options.D: Improvement of renal blood flow

question: How is community health nursing different from working inside a hospital ward?

options.C: It operates strictly inside enclosed clinic wards

question: How should you respond as a nurse if a client worries that injectable contraceptives will make her permanently barren?

question: What crucial advice must a nurse give to a male patient who has just recovered from Ebola?

question: How are direct-acting smooth muscle relaxants different from anticholinergics?

question: What is a major risk of maintaining unsafe patient-to-nurse ratios?

question: A patient has an infected open leg fracture that hasn't healed over the past eight months, despite short courses of oral antibiotics. What type of osteomyelitis is this?

question: Why is keeping a close eye on blood pressure so important right after brain surgery?

question: A nurse wants to travel abroad for an 18-month post-basic nursing degree while keeping their job. What should they apply for?

question: What big problem can happen with combined city sewer systems during heavy rainstorms?

question: What are the three fundamental pillars that drive population dynamics?

question: Why do low-income communities often suffer more deaths during natural disasters?

question: What is the main goal of primary health care (PHC) services in Nigeria?

question: Why is supporting family caregivers considered such a vital part of home healthcare?

question: Which nutrient is especially helpful for building collagen and healing bones?

question: What is the main job of enzymes in our metabolism?

question: What crucial instruction should a nurse give to a pregnant woman diagnosed with a low-lying placenta (placenta praevia)?

question: The AED just delivered a shock to your patient. What is the very next thing your team should do?

question: How does continuous on-the-job training help primary healthcare workers?

explanation: Regular training boosts your confidence and makes sure you are up-to-date with the latest and best ways to care for your patients. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T4#GNS124_U2_T4_h7)

question: What was Linda Richards' big contribution to psychiatric care?

question: Why is an elderly patient with poorly controlled diabetes at a much higher risk for a slow-healing foot infection?

question: Why is a 'Theory Y' leadership style usually much better for registered nurses than Theory X?

question: What is the thermic effect of food?

question: A study tests if a new low-salt diet lowers blood pressure in hypertensive patients. What is the independent variable?

question: What is the main purpose of advance care planning?

options.C: To calculate the total financial cost of hospital treatment
options.D: To schedule nursing shifts for the upcoming week

explanation: Advance care planning lets people make their medical wishes known while they are still able to, ensuring their voice is respected even if they get too sick to speak later. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T5#GNS321_U3_T5_h9)

question: Which of these is NOT a direct complication of an unsafe or incomplete abortion?

question: What is one exciting benefit expected from future voice-activated documentation tools?

question: What is a common danger when researchers use very long or complex checklists during busy ward shifts?

question: A teenager avoids emergency contraception because she believes it causes permanent infertility. What type of barrier is this?

question: Why have state governments in Nigeria introduced State Health Insurance Agencies alongside the federal scheme?

question: Why are mid-range servers (minicomputers) so helpful in hospital departments like the laboratory?

question: Why must a nursing school periodically evaluate its instructional materials?

question: What is the main difference between an acute care EHR and an ambulatory EHR?

question: Which communication style involves stating your professional concerns clearly without being aggressive or overly timid?

question: Why should a nurse check lab results before confirming neurasthenia?

question: How can community health nurses best encourage rural women to seek early help for breast lumps?

options.C: By engaging local leaders and providing culturally sensitive education

question: How does real-time data access in an EHR help protect patients?

question: What is the best way to write down a skin problem in a patient's nursing chart?

question: What is the main risk of poor water management in heavily irrigated dry lands over time?

question: A patient in a disaster zone has a severe head injury, is unresponsive, breathing irregularly, and has no pulse. Which triage category fits best?

question: Which of these is NOT a typical daytime sign of chronic insomnia?

question: How should nurses view technology in home health care?

question: Why do some women still seek out traditional practitioners for gishiri cuts instead of going to a hospital?

question: Which mental health condition is frequently missed in older adults because it often hides behind physical complaints like body aches?

question: Why are bedside nurses usually the best people to spot where clinical changes are needed?

question: Why is a quick review session important right after finishing a community disaster simulation?

question: Why is a nutrition history considered a vital part of a standard patient admission assessment?

question: Why do we often view rural villagers and urban slum residents as vulnerable populations?

question: When you look at a bedside cardiac monitor, what is it mainly showing you?

question: What is the main goal of conducting a community health assessment?

question: What is the main focus of end-of-life care when a patient is being cared for at home?

question: What is the main purpose of doing a Root Cause Analysis after a mistake happens?

question: Why don't we usually place supercomputers at a patient's bedside in a general ward?

question: What is the primary role of laboratory reports in microbial surveillance?

question: Which prevention method helps protect vulnerable people in the community who cannot receive vaccines themselves?

question: Why are routine screenings, like annual tuberculosis tests, so important for hospital staff?
